data.title: Mechanical Pencil
data.solution:
# Get the length of the pencil's led after executing all steps.
width = int(input())
led = int(input())
n = int(input())
for i in range(n):
  command = input()
  if command == "PRESS":
    led += 1
  elif command == "CLOSE":
    led = 0
  else:
    led -= int(command.split()[1])
    if led < 0:
      led = 0

# Print the pencil.
print(f'+{"-" * (width - 3)}\\')
print(f'|{" " * (width - 2)}|{"-" * led}')
print(f'+{"-" * (width - 3)}/')
data.statement:
Output a mechanical pencil after executing all [[n]] steps, represented by [[command]]. The length of the pencil's led starts at [[led]], and [[width]] represents the width of the pencil without its led.

<<Commands:>>
{{PRESS}} - Increases the length of the pencil's led by {{1}}.
{{CLOSE}} - Sets the led's length to {{0}}.
{{PUSH}} always followed by <<the push power>>, separated by a space - Decreases the length of the pencil's led by <<the push power>>.

<<How to Draw the Pencil:>> (recommended to check the example output if still confused)
<<1)>> A {{+}} followed by ([[width]] - {{3}}) {{-}}'s, then followed by a backslash {{\}}.
<<2)>> A {{|}} followed by ([[width]] - {{2}}) spaces followed by another {{|}}, then followed by trailing {{-}}'s of the length of the pencil after executing all [[n]] commands.
<<3)>> A {{+}} followed by ([[width]] - {{3}}) {{-}}'s, then followed by a forward slash {{/}}.

<<Note:>> The led's length never goes below {{0}}. If you get a {{PUSH}} command whose push power is greater than the led's current length, then just treat it like a {{CLOSE}} command.

Good luck! ;)

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

Output a mechanical pencil after executing all n steps, represented by command. The length of the pencil's led starts at led, and width represents the width of the pencil without its led.

Commands:
PRESS - Increases the length of the pencil's led by 1.
CLOSE - Sets the led's length to 0.
PUSH always followed by the push power, separated by a space - Decreases the length of the pencil's led by the push power.

How to Draw the Pencil: (recommended to check the example output if still confused)
1) A + followed by (width - 3) -'s, then followed by a backslash \.
2) A | followed by (width - 2) spaces followed by another |, then followed by trailing -'s of the length of the pencil after executing all n commands.
3) A + followed by (width - 3) -'s, then followed by a forward slash /.

Note: The led's length never goes below 0. If you get a PUSH command whose push power is greater than the led's current length, then just treat it like a CLOSE command.

Good luck! ;)
Input
Line 1: An integer width representing the width of the mechanical pencil without its led.
Line 2: An integer led representing the starting length of the mechanical pencil's led.
Line 3: An integer n representing the number of commands.
Next n lines: A string command representing the command to execute. Either PRESS, CLOSE, or PUSH followed by the push power.
Output
The mechanical pencil after following the steps in the statement. There will always be 3 lines of output.
Constraints
3 ≤ width ≤ 20
0 ≤ led ≤ 20
1 ≤ n ≤ 15
command is only the options listed in the statement.
Example
Input
5
0
3
PRESS
PRESS
PRESS
Output
+--\
|   |---
+--/
